A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HiFo-Prompt. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original heuristic evaluations on TSP, online bin packing, flow-shop scheduling, and Bayesian optimization, alongside component ablations and efficiency measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark results and adds experiments across LLMs, parameter sensitivity studies, mechanism ablations, and statistical summaries.

M1.justification: The architecture and prompt operators remain. However, Section 3.3 replaces fitness-standard-deviation diversity with the fraction of algorithm-description pairs having unequal text. Section 3.2 also revises credit-assignment inequalities and introduces numerical stabilization and clipping. These change parts of the documented procedure without replacing the framework.

E1.justification: The four problem families and existing benchmark collections remain. TSP-GLS evaluation changes from 50/100/200-node instances to 100/200/500-node instances. Small construction cases are retained in v2 Table 7 rather than removed; the additional LLM and parameter configurations do not introduce new task families.

E2.justification: Comparator membership changes within retained experiments: POMO and LEHD move from the GLS comparison into construction comparisons, while GLS gains ReEvo and an explicit LKH3 row. The appendix BPP table drops Funsearch, although main Table 3 retains it. The cost comparison replaces HSEvo with MCTS-AHD.

E3.justification: Section 4 changes the stated population size from 4 to 8. New protocols evaluate five underlying LLMs and systematically vary search and memory parameters. Evaluation also adds heuristic execution times and input/output token consumption, substantially extending the experimental design beyond the original benchmark and component comparisons.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component-removal ablations, Appendices C.5-C.7 add cross-LLM robustness tests, eight-parameter sensitivity analysis, seed-insight controls for baselines, adaptive versus fixed-Balance comparisons, regime-frequency analysis, and utility/reward ablations. These directly investigate portability, architectural necessity, and internal mechanisms.

E5.justification: v1 already labels its efficiency figure as averaged over five runs. v2 newly specifies three-run averages for main benchmark tables and additional studies, and Table 18 reports individual runs and standard deviations across representative tasks and methods. This broadens statistical reporting without establishing a general increase in repetitions.

E6.justification: Many benchmark and ablation entries change: HiFo-Prompt's TSP50 construction gap changes from 5.808% to 6.625%, and BPP 5k_C100 from 0.66% to 0.69%. Extensive new robustness, ablation, runtime, and token results appear. TSPLib and BO scores remain unchanged. Revised settings and aggregation preclude interpreting updated scores as same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: The formal diversity definition changes, normalization gains an epsilon term, and Eq. 3 reverses its inequalities to agree with the maximized-fitness formulation in Appendix A.1. Credit clipping and a sliding-window recency formula are also specified. These are operational mathematical revisions; no theorem or proof development is added.

C1.justification: The contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: complementary Hindsight/Foresight modules, reusable knowledge, adaptive search control, superior AHD performance, and query efficiency. The revised abstract and symbolic-meta-optimizer framing do not materially change those claims.

C2.justification: New discussion attributes performance to adaptive regime switching, knowledge management rather than seed quality alone, balanced utility components, and compatibility between framework and LLM. Existing controller and cross-task-transfer limitations remain. One new interpretation is incorrect: Table 13 shows MCTS-AHD improving with seeds in all five cases, although the prose cites it as deteriorating.

D1.justification: v2 adds a repository pointer, CPU specification, text preprocessing and recency-window details, and four generated-heuristic code listings. Appendix B.1 clarifies offline synthesis versus heuristic execution. Conversely, v1's framework and selection pseudocode disappears, along with its explicit API and temperature disclosure. These substantially alter the available reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The introduction and related work substantially reposition HiFo-Prompt against model fine-tuning approaches such as EvoTune and CALM, and distinguish MoH and RedAHD as addressing other dimensions. Numerous earlier background citations are removed, while new discussion connects recency management to sliding-window bandit methods.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and substantial method passages are rewritten. Appendix B.1 receives a significant explanatory correction, comparative discussion moves into expanded appendices, and appendix organization changes. Author information, acknowledgments, and an LLM writing-assistance disclosure are also revised or added.

P2.justification: Benchmark tables are split or restructured and gain runtime or objective columns. The retained convergence plot moves to the appendix; v1's efficiency plot is replaced by v2's cost table, while a new sensitivity figure and numerous analysis tables appear. Figures 1-2 largely retain their artwork.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for robustness and the proposed mechanisms through cross-LLM tests, parameter and controlled ablations, and explicit run-level variability. Runtime/token reporting and generated code make costs and outputs more inspectable. Removal of framework pseudocode and the incorrect Table 13 interpretation are meaningful drawbacks, but the broader, more diagnostic validation provides a substantial net improvement.
